title: Pricing writes by what they cost the database
subtitle: An admission controller that reads the database's own pressure, write-ahead-log rate, active writers and lock waits, and admits work only as fast as the database can take it

stats.label: pressure signals, all read from the database's own statistics
lattice-wide function running inside the database at a time

lede: GPU-scale producers can push a database into trouble long before any query fails. The write path described in A write path that sizes itself keeps the database from being hammered by individual workers; the admission controller keeps the whole fleet from exceeding what the database can absorb. A sampler reads the database's own statistics, the write-ahead log, its writers, its locks and its statement statistics. Each signal is normalised between a healthy level and a critical one, and the signals are combined into one pressure index. The weights are tuned to this estate and stay private; the shape of the index does not.
quote: It measures the database and spends the measurement.
evidence: Database admission control: an admission controller that combines 4 pressure signals from the database's own statistics, write-ahead log, writers, locks and statement statistics, into one pressure index for a GPU-scale fleet.

Rate limiting: token buckets in log bytes, rows and write slots per lane and per schema that refill in full, partly or not at all by pressure band, with an atomic admit-or-hold check in the queue store.

Distributed systems correctness: lattice-wide in-database functions held to 1 at a time under a lock with a heartbeat and a time-to-live, so a crashed holder cannot block the lane and a stale one cannot release it.
Shadow-mode rollout: 3 modes, off, shadow and enforce, with shadow mode logging every decision without holding anything, so thresholds were set against real load before any write was refused.
Multi-tenant fairness: schemas take turns so one tenant cannot monopolise the buckets, waiting batches gain priority with age, and a slow function throttles only its own writes.
author: Corey James
